root_cause.text: In the tw9903_probe() function, when write_regs() fails, the error path returns without freeing the v4l2 control handler that was previously allocated by v4l2_ctrl_handler_init() and v4l2_ctrl_new_std(), causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `v4l2_ctrl_handler_free(hdl);` inside the error handling block after `if (write_regs(sd, initial_registers) < 0)`, matching the CVE description that an error path fails to free the control handler's allocated memory.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the tw9903_probe() function, after successfully initializing the v4l2_ctrl_handler via v4l2_ctrl_handler_init() and v4l2_ctrl_new_std(), and assigning it to sd->ctrl_handler, the error path when write_regs() fails (lines 259-261) only calls kfree(dec) but does not call v4l2_ctrl_handler_free(&dec->hdl). This causes a memory leak of the control handler. The fix should add v4l2_ctrl_handler_free(hdl) before kfree(dec) in that error path.
